verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every scale of (6.1) is defined, in the direction the paper writes, but spread over several declarations rather than one. Identical: Q = 2^{-ℓ} (dyadicQ, with the dyadic index as a natural number n in place of ℓ), ε = Q^h (epsilon), S_* = ℓ² (S n = n²), D = 1/2 − h (CoordinateAlgebra.D). The physical-to-chart map is PhysicalGraphBounds.chartLinear, whose docstring calls it the "Cartesian form of the exact chart (T, R cos θ, R sin θ, Z)": chartLinear_apply gives the components (−Q^{-1}·t, (Q^{-1/2}·x, (Q^{-1/2}·y, Q^{-D h}·z))). The two space slots carry Q^{-1/2} on the Cartesian (x,y), so their norm is r/√Q, which is R = r/√Q; the third is Z = z/Q^D verbatim, with D h = 1/2 − h. The same radial scaling is also packaged on its own as scaledRadial n = Q^{-1/2} • radialProjection (radialProjection p = (p.2 0, p.2 1)), with inverse unscale_radial. For the time slot, physicalChart adds Q^{-1} to chartLinear's first component, and physicalChart_time states (physicalChart h n p).1 = (1 − p.1)/Q n, which is T = τ/Q with τ = 1 − t, as a theorem. So the only gap is packaging: no single declaration bundles the seven assignments, and the dyadic exponent is a natural number n rather than the paper's ℓ. Secondary remark: the band chart of SimilarityHomogeneity encodes the same scalings in the opposite direction and in a squared radial slot, chartToPhysical h Q (R,(Z,T)) = (1 − Q·T, (Q·R²/2, Q^D·Z)); chartToPhysical_radial (hypothesis 0 < Q only) gives the radial slot s = (√Q·R)²/2, from which r = √Q·R needs the square-root step and hence R ≥ 0, which the paper's annulus supplies.
